subject: literature
passage: On the morning of his last day, Rahmat Ali climbed the rope ladder up the freighter's side as he had done some nine thousand times before, nodded to the captain on the bridge, and took his place beside the helmsman. The Karnaphuli ran brown and quick with the tide. He called the turns without looking at a chart: the shoal off the old jetty, the bend where the current set hard toward the eastern bank. Forty years earlier, on his first passage, his hands had shaken so badly that the senior pilot had made him hold them behind his back. Now, as the berths of Chittagong came into view, he turned to the young pilot who had been shadowing him all week and, without a word, stepped aside to let him call the final turn.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It follows a man through a familiar task, recalls his beginnings, and ends as he hands it to a successor.
choices.B: It introduces a young pilot, traces the stages of his training, and ends with his first passage without supervision.
choices.C: It contrasts two rivers on which a pilot has worked and explains why he has come to prefer one of them.
choices.D: It describes a dangerous passage up a river, explains what went wrong, and shows the pilot accepting the blame.

explanation.why: The passage follows Rahmat Ali through a routine he has repeated "some nine thousand times," pauses to recall his nervous first passage "forty years earlier," and ends with him stepping aside so "the young pilot" can call the final turn. The structure is familiar task, memory of beginnings, handing on of the task.
explanation.A: Correct. The routine passage, the memory of his first voyage, and his stepping aside for the young pilot occur in that order.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The young pilot appears only at the end; the passage centers on Rahmat Ali and never traces anyone's training.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Only one river, the Karnaphuli, is described.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing goes wrong in the passage; Rahmat Ali calls the turns with ease.
